reviewer_concern: Why use a neural model if EdgeBank achieves higher AP on real datasets?
manuscript_response: EdgeBank memorizes exact node pairs (u v) and collapses when edge overlap is low (AP 0.5774 in Condition B); our paper explicitly decomposes exact vs structural recurrence to show where structural models matter.
remaining_limitation: EdgeBank remains superior when exact pairwise edges repeat.
exact_wording_to_use: Exact-edge memorization explains much of the signal when node pairs repeat; structural recurrence isolates historical predictive organization beyond exact pair overlap.

reviewer_concern: Isn't this identical to standard continual graph learning?
manuscript_response: Continual graph learning studies sequential tasks/classes with changing objectives; our setting keeps the link prediction task fixed while interaction regimes switch and recur in a continuous event stream.
remaining_limitation: Conceptually related but experimentally and mathematically distinct.
exact_wording_to_use: Although related to catastrophic forgetting our setting differs because the prediction task remains fixed while the temporal interaction regime recurs.

attack_name: This is just long-term dependency modeling.
reviewer_concern: Isn't this the same as long-range temporal attention (e.g. DyGFormer)?
manuscript_response: Long-range attention models historical interactions within a single continuous regime; our protocol isolates the specific interference caused by intervening conflicting dynamics (A->B->A).
remaining_limitation: Transformers scale context length at quadratic compute/memory cost.
exact_wording_to_use: Our controlled protocol isolates the behavior of finite recurrent-state compression; long-history sequence models represent complementary mechanisms for historical access.

reviewer_concern: CRAFT (NeurIPS 2025) proves memory-free models beat memory-based models so why study memory?
manuscript_response: CRAFT asks whether explicit memory is necessary for forward forecasting on standard benchmarks; our paper asks what historically predictive information remains recoverable in recurrent memory after conflicting regimes.
remaining_limitation: Our work is diagnostic of recurrent representation behavior rather than a claim of memory necessity.
exact_wording_to_use: Our study is diagnostic of historical representation accessibility rather than a claim that recurrent memory is universally required.

attack_name: Why not a Transformer over entire history?
reviewer_concern: Why use episodic checkpoints instead of full-history self-attention?
manuscript_response: Full-history attention requires storing and processing unbounded historical edge sequences (quadratic complexity); MA-TGN bounds memory to K=10 checkpoints (827.5 KB) with sub-5 us latency.
remaining_limitation: Full-history attention may capture uncompressed history if compute is unbounded.
exact_wording_to_use: Addressable episodic memory provides a sublinear bounded alternative to full-history sequence attention.

attack_name: Retrieval module is just another external memory.
reviewer_concern: Memory-augmented networks already exist in NLP and static graphs so what is new?
manuscript_response: We do not claim episodic memory itself is novel; our contribution is using addressable episodic memory as a diagnostic intervention to characterize historical recoverability in dynamic graphs.
remaining_limitation: External memory mechanisms require checkpoint scheduling and query routing.
exact_wording_to_use: We introduce addressable episodic memory as an architectural intervention to test whether historical information remains externally recoverable when overwritten in recurrent states.

attack_name: Four recurrence episodes are too few.
reviewer_concern: Can you claim real-world generalization from n=4 episodes per dataset?
manuscript_response: We explicitly treat n=4 natural episodes as qualitative supporting analogues and avoid overstating inferential population claims.
remaining_limitation: Limited statistical sample size on real-world datasets.
exact_wording_to_use: Across the four evaluated recurrence episodes in CollegeMsg and Bitcoin-OTC MA-TGN consistently outperforms Continuous TGN providing supportive qualitative evidence.

reviewer_concern: The discrete Dynamic SBM benchmark is idealized and does not reflect complex real-world graphs.
manuscript_response: The synthetic benchmark deliberately isolates distractor duration TB and community persistence to provide controlled causal measurements impossible in noisy observational data.
remaining_limitation: Real graphs have overlapping continuous multi-scale transitions.
exact_wording_to_use: The controlled synthetic benchmark isolates the causal relationship between distractor duration and historical recoverability under clean structural invariants.

reviewer_concern: Did you tune TGN properly or is it crippled?
manuscript_response: Continuous TGN was evaluated across 10 random seeds using standard Adam optimizer (lr=0.005) matching canonical literature baselines within 0.005 AP tolerance.
remaining_limitation: Neural message passing on unfeatured graphs must learn structural invariants from scratch.
exact_wording_to_use: Unfeatured neural models converge to ~0.652 AP while heuristic common-neighbor probes achieve ~0.760 AP by directly computing topological intersection counts.

reviewer_concern: Is the historical oracle a formal mathematical upper bound?
manuscript_response: The Historical Oracle is a diagnostic reference accessing the ground-truth historical summary graph rather than a formal theoretical ceiling.
remaining_limitation: A hypothetical omniscient predictor could combine current and historical graphs.
exact_wording_to_use: The Historical Oracle serves as an empirical structural reference rather than a formal mathematical upper bound.
